topic.title: Your phone's two location choices (Android)
topic.question: When an Android app asks for your location, what exactly are you choosing?

intent.whoThisHelps: Android users who tap through location prompts without knowing what they allow.
intent.whatTheyLearn: Android location access has two separate choices: when (foreground or background) and how exact (precise or approximate).
intent.whatTheyCanDo: Review which apps have location all the time, and give approximate location where exact location isn't needed.
intent.whyEvidenceSupportsIt: Google's Android developer documentation describes the permission model directly.
intent.whatEvidenceDoesNotEstablish: It does not say how individual apps use location once granted, does not cover iPhone, and menu names can differ by phone maker and Android version.

claims.text: Android location permissions combine two characteristics: a category (foreground or background) and an accuracy (precise or approximate).
claims.limitations: Describes the permission model; exact on-screen wording varies by Android version and phone maker.
claims.singleOriginJustification: Platform behaviour is defined by the platform owner: Android's official developer documentation is the authoritative source for how Android's own permission system works. Recheck the page before publication.

claims.text: On Android 11 and higher, the permission dialog does not include the 'Allow all the time' option; users must enable background location on a settings page.
claims.limitations: Applies to Android 11 (API level 30) and higher; Android 10 showed the option in the dialog.
claims.singleOriginJustification: Platform behaviour is defined by the platform owner: Android's official developer documentation is the authoritative source for how Android's own permission system works. Recheck the page before publication.

claims.text: If the user grants only approximate location, the app has only approximate location, including in the background.
claims.limitations: Concerns the location permission itself; it does not cover other ways an app might estimate location.
claims.singleOriginJustification: Platform behaviour is defined by the platform owner: Android's official developer documentation is the authoritative source for how Android's own permission system works. Recheck the page before publication.

claims.text: On Android 10 and higher, the first time an app accesses location in the background after the user grants background access, the system schedules a notification reminding the user they allowed location all the time.
claims.limitations: Android 10 (API level 29) and higher; the reminder is sent once, on first background use.
claims.singleOriginJustification: Platform behaviour is defined by the platform owner: Android's official developer documentation is the authoritative source for how Android's own permission system works. Recheck the page before publication.

claims.text: Android treats an app as using foreground location when one of its activities is visible or when it is running a foreground service, which shows a persistent notification; with a foreground service it keeps access after the user presses Home or turns the screen off.
claims.limitations: Developer-facing definition; what users see in settings may be labelled differently.
claims.singleOriginJustification: Platform behaviour is defined by the platform owner: Android's official developer documentation is the authoritative source for how Android's own permission system works. Recheck the page before publication.

evidence.supportingPassage: Each permission has a combination of the following characteristics: Category: Either foreground location or background location. Accuracy: Either precise location or approximate location.

On Android 11 (API level 30) and higher, however, the system dialog doesn't include the Allow all the time option. Instead, users must enable background location on a settings page, as shown in figure 7.
If the user grants the approximate location permission, your app only has access to approximate location, regardless of which location permissions your app declares.

if the user grants your app the ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION permission but grants only approximate location access in the foreground, your app has only approximate location access in the background as well.
evidence.locator: Section: User can affect background location accuracy

evidence.supportingPassage: On Android 10 (API level 29) and higher, when a feature in your app accesses device location in the background for the first time after the user grants background location access, the system schedules a notification to send to the user. This notification reminds the user that they've allowed your app to access device location all the time.
evidence.locator: Section: Reminder of background location grant

evidence.supportingPassage: The system considers your app to be using foreground location if a feature of your app accesses the device's current location in one of the following situations: An activity that belongs to your app is visible. Your app is running a foreground service. When a foreground service is running, the system raises user awareness by showing a persistent notification. Your app retains access when it's placed in the background, such as when the user presses the Home button on their device or turns their device's display off.
